title: Cross-Border Cases and Mock Hearing Workshop
summary: Brings the programme together by examining mutual legal assistance and foreign evidence, ending with a mock hearing in which participants argue and decide the key issues in a laundering case.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together by examining mutual legal assistance and foreign evidence, ending with a mock hearing in which participants argue and decide the key issues in a laundering case.
Learning Objectives: Draft effective mutual legal assistance requests for evidence and assets
Manage the admissibility and use of evidence obtained abroad
Apply the programme to argue and decide a realistic case
Syllabus: Mutual legal assistance: dual criminality, content and timing
Joint investigation teams and direct cooperation between prosecutors
Admissibility and use of foreign evidence
Workshop: mock hearing on knowledge, evidence and confiscation
Intended Audience: Prosecutors handling money laundering, fraud, corruption and other economic crime
Judges and magistrates hearing financial crime, restraint and confiscation cases
Senior investigators and legal advisers who prepare financial crime cases for prosecution
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience of criminal prosecution, judicial work or financial crime investigation is helpful. No accounting or technical background is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2012, as updated), International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations
UNODC (2012), Manual on Mutual Legal Assistance and Extradition
World Bank and UNODC StAR Initiative (2021), Asset Recovery Handbook: A Guide for Practitioners, Second Edition
